Question Choices: A line that divides a figure into two matching reflected halves is called what?
Question Answers: line of symmetry|axis of symmetry|a line of symmetry|an axis of symmetry
Hints: Folding along this line makes the halves coincide.|It is also called a reflection axis.
Solution: It is a line of symmetry, also called an axis of symmetry. Reflection across this line maps every point of the figure onto a point of the same figure.

Question Choices: How many lines of symmetry does a nonsquare rectangle have?
Hints: Consider the vertical and horizontal midlines.|Diagonal folds do not match unless the rectangle is a square.
Solution: A nonsquare rectangle has two reflection axes: the lines through the center parallel to its sides. A diagonal would exchange unequal adjacent side lengths, so diagonals are not symmetry lines.

Question Choices: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
Hints: Count two midlines and two diagonals.|Each fold maps the square onto itself.
Solution: A square has four reflection axes: two lines joining opposite side midpoints and its two diagonals. Each reflects the entire square onto itself.

Question Choices: What is the smallest positive rotation that maps a square onto itself about its center?
Hints: A square has rotational symmetry of order 4.|Divide 360 degrees by 4.
Solution: The regular polygon has 4 equally spaced vertices. The smallest matching turn advances one vertex position, so its angle is 360/4 = 90 degrees.

Question Choices: Select. A parallelogram is rotated 180 degrees about the intersection of its diagonals. Does it map onto itself? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Opposite vertices switch places.|A parallelogram has half-turn symmetry.
Solution: Yes. Parallelogram diagonals bisect each other. Their intersection is the midpoint of each opposite vertex pair, so a half-turn exchanges opposite vertices and sides and preserves the entire outline.

Question Choices: Reflecting a figure over one line and then over a perpendicular intersecting line is equivalent to a rotation of how many degrees?
Hints: Two intersecting-line reflections make a rotation.|Double the 90-degree angle between the lines.
Solution: Two reflections across intersecting lines make a rotation through twice their angle. Perpendicular lines meet at 90 degrees, so the turn is 2 × 90 = 180 degrees about their intersection.

Question Choices: Select. When two lines intersect are vertical angles congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Each vertical angle is supplementary to the same adjacent angle.|Angles with equal supplements are equal.
Solution: Vertical angles lie opposite at the intersection. Each is supplementary to the same adjacent angle. Subtracting that common angle from 180 degrees gives equal measures, so vertical angles are congruent.

Question Choices: Perpendicular lines form angles of what measure?
Hints: Perpendicular means meeting at right angles.|A right angle is one quarter-turn.
Solution: By definition, perpendicular lines meet at right angles. Each of the four angles at the intersection is 90 degrees.

Question Choices: Two adjacent angles form a straight line. Their measures sum to how many degrees?
Hints: They form a linear pair.|A straight angle measures 180 degrees.
Solution: The two adjacent angles form a linear pair: their outer rays point in opposite directions. Together they make a straight angle, so their measures add to 180 degrees.

Question Choices: Select. A reflection maps two perpendicular lines to their images. Are the image lines still perpendicular? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Reflections preserve angle measure.|The 90-degree angle remains 90 degrees.
Solution: Yes. Reflection preserves angle measure. The original lines meet at 90 degrees, so their images also meet at 90 degrees and remain perpendicular.
